newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity finishes higher after up week.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity finishes higher after up week.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures finished higher Friday on some strong buying interest, capping a week of climbing values, industry sources said.
"We saw some strong buying interest late in the day and it seems to have scared the whole complex higher," said one Houston-based futures trader.
May Palo Verde (PV) finished up 31 cents at $15.45 per megawatt hour (MWh) after trade in a range of $15.10-15.50, while June closed up 40 cents at $16.54 after trading at $16.15-16.60 per MWh.
Deferreds were also higher, with August settling up 11 cents at $24.50 per MWh.
May California Oregon Border (COB) ended up 40 cents at $11.50 after trade as low as $10.90, while June closed up 22 cents at $11.61 from trade in a range of $11.15-11.70 per MWh.
August COB finished up 19 cents at $18.19 after trade at $18.05-18.35 per MWh.
NYMEX said an estimated 578 PV and 463 COB contracts traded.
Sources said electricity futures could ease early next week following the rise through this week.
"We have had a pretty good run here, and we might some a little weakness early next week," one futures trader said.

Earlier in the day, sources had said electricity futures may be taking some strength from talk of hydropower production being pushed back with flows on the Columbia River possibly being lower than expected over the short term due to cool weather.

Temperatures in the Northwest were forecast to range widely from two degrees Fahrenheit above normal near the southern coast to as much as 12 degrees below normal in the far northeast area over the next several days.
Readings would also vary throughout the Southwest, averaging about two degrees above normal in the northwest corner to five degrees below normal in the southeast region.
In the West, the 1,070 megawatt (MW) San Onofre 2 nuclear unit in southern California reached 100 percent power Thursday night.
The 1,221 MW Palo Verde 3 nuclear power unit in Arizona continued to ramp toward full output, with 100 percent production expected to be achieved this weekend.
Meanwhile, the 1,073 MW Diablo Canyon unit 2 on the coast of central California was expected to reconnect to the electricity grid today after being shut last Saturday to repair a feedwater pump line.
